cases.n: Brazil — Joint Congressional Inquiry (CPMI) into networks sexually exploiting children (2004)
cases.who: Networks including politicians, businessmen, judges and clergy named by the commission
cases.d: A joint commission of 11 senators and 11 deputies, created in 2003 to investigate violence and networks of sexual exploitation of children and adolescents, received more than 800 complaints and heard about 300 people in 14 states. Its final report, approved on 13 July 2004, put more than 250 people on notice, among them 20 serving politicians (one federal deputy, two state deputies and three mayors), about 30 businessmen and five priests, and passed the cases to federal and state prosecutors. It recommended reclassifying 'offences against public morals' as sexual crimes and making internal trafficking of adolescents a crime.
cases.cite: Relatório final da Comissão Parlamentar Mista de Inquérito da exploração sexual de crianças e adolescentes (Senator Patrícia Saboya, president; Deputy Maria do Rosário, rapporteur), 2004; Senate speech of Sen. Patrícia Saboya, 12 May 2004; Al Jazeera, 17 July 2004

cases.n: Brazil — Senate 'CPI da Pedofilia' on online abuse material and child abuse (2008–2010)
cases.who: Users of the Orkut social network and offenders across Brazil; a Pará state deputy convicted after testimony
cases.d: The Federal Senate's parliamentary inquiry into paedophilia, chaired by Senator Magno Malta, worked for almost three years and delivered a final report of about 1,700 pages to the Federal Police and federal prosecutors in December 2010. It signed a conduct agreement with Google, the Federal Police and prosecutors to lift secrecy on Orkut pages linked to child abuse. Rádio Senado reported that hundreds of people were arrested or indicted after its work, and that a state deputy from Belém was convicted and jailed for abusing children after testifying. Laws passed during its work criminalised possession of child abuse material and closed businesses where children were exploited.
cases.cite: Federal Senate, CPI da Pedofilia final report (December 2010), as reported by Rádio Senado, 13 and 16 December 2010

cases.n: Brazil — Chamber of Deputies inquiry asks indictment of 37, including a mayor and state deputies (2014)
cases.who: Local politicians and others in Amazonas, Minas Gerais and other states
cases.d: A parliamentary inquiry of the Chamber of Deputies, installed in 2012 with Deputy Liliam Sá as rapporteur, approved its final report on 4 June 2014. It asked for the indictment of 37 people for sexual exploitation of children and adolescents, among them the mayor of Coari (Amazonas), Adail Pinheiro, a serving Amazonas state deputy, a former state deputy and a former president of the Três Corações city council.
cases.cite: Câmara dos Deputados, CPI Exploração Sexual de Crianças e Adolescentes, final report approved 4 June 2014, as reported by Congresso em Foco

cases.n: Argentina — CONADEP 'Nunca Más': children of the disappeared taken and given to military families (1984)
cases.victims_note: report: no fewer than 200 children under 15 kidnapped; 8,961 disappearances recorded in all
cases.cover: Identities of children changed; records of births in detention not kept
cases.d: The National Commission on the Disappearance of Persons, created by President Raúl Alfonsín on 15 December 1983 and chaired by Ernesto Sábato, delivered its report Nunca Más on 20 September 1984. It recorded 8,961 forced disappearances and stated that no fewer than 200 children under 15 had been kidnapped; babies were taken with their parents or born to pregnant prisoners in detention camps and handed to military families. The report was the first official finding of the practice later judged a 'systematic plan' in 2012.
cases.cite: Comisión Nacional sobre la Desaparición de Personas, Nunca Más, 20 September 1984 (via Wikipedia and Encyclopedia of Latin American History and Culture)

cases.n: Chile — National Prosecutor's Office: 166 investigations of clergy and church workers, 248 victims (2019)
cases.victims_note: 131 of the 248 were children or adolescents when abused; 35 adults; no information for 82
cases.who: Catholic clergy, religious and lay church workers; 10 bishops investigated
cases.d: After the 2018 Scicluna mission, Chile's National Prosecutor's Office opened a national review of sexual abuse in the Catholic Church, with raids on diocesan offices. Its balance of 30 April 2019 counted 166 open or closed investigations, 221 people investigated, including 10 bishops (mostly for alleged cover-up), and 248 victims, of whom 131 were children or adolescents.
cases.cite: Fiscalía Nacional de Chile, balance of investigations into members of the Catholic Church, 30 April 2019, as reported by El Dínamo

cases.n: Chile — Chamber of Deputies commission on irregular adoptions (2019)
cases.who: Hospital medical and paramedical staff, Civil Registry staff, private intermediary organisations
cases.cover: Hospital birth records for 1970–1990 missing or destroyed
cases.d: A special investigating commission of the Chamber of Deputies, chaired by Deputy Boris Barrera, worked from January to 22 July 2019 on children taken from mainly poor, often rural mothers, who were frequently told their babies had died, and sent for adoption, many abroad, before, during and after the 1973–1990 dictatorship. It found complicity by medical and paramedical staff and Civil Registry staff, and that private intermediaries were the main channel and were paid. It recommended an international DNA bank, a national truth commission on irregular adoptions and excluding private bodies from adoption; the Chamber approved the report in October 2019.
cases.cite: Cámara de Diputados de Chile, Comisión Especial Investigadora sobre adopciones irregulares, report of July 2019 (approved October 2019), as reported by El Desconcierto

cases.n: Ecuador — National Assembly 'AAMPETRA' commission on sexual violence in schools (2018)
cases.victims_note: named after the Academia Aeronáutica Mayor Pedro Traversari in Quito, where 41 children were abused; government data later showed 4,221 pupils suffered sexual violence in schools 2014–May 2020 (HRW analysis)
cases.who: Teachers and staff of public and private schools; Ministry of Education
cases.cover: Commission found negligence by public institutions, the Ministry of Education and judicial authorities
cases.d: Ecuador's National Assembly set up a multiparty occasional commission in 2017 after families of pupils abused at the Academia Aeronáutica Mayor Pedro Traversari (AAMPETRA) in Quito, where 41 children were abused, mobilised. It reviewed cases from 2013 to 2017 and, in a report approved unanimously on 16 February 2018, found negligence by public institutions, the Ministry of Education and judicial authorities and concluded that former ministers had not acted. Human Rights Watch's later analysis of government data counted 4,221 pupils who suffered sexual violence in schools between 2014 and May 2020.
cases.cite: Asamblea Nacional del Ecuador, Comisión Especializada Ocasional AAMPETRA, report approved 16 February 2018; Human Rights Watch, 9 December 2020

cases.n: Jamaica — Keating Report on children in state care finds sexual abuse by caregivers (2003)
cases.who: Jamaican children's homes and places of safety; Child Services Division
cases.cover: Nine of 15 homes visited could not recall an official inspection in the previous three years
cases.d: The Government of Jamaica appointed a four-member review panel chaired by Sadie Keating in December 2002, after a public campaign about abuse in children's homes. Its report, made public in July 2003, found that children in homes and places of safety had been sexually abused, including by care-givers, and that nine of the 15 homes visited could not recall a Child Services Division inspection in three years.
cases.cite: Report on the Situation of Children in the Care of the Jamaican State (Keating Report), 2003, as reported by the Jamaica Observer, 15 July 2003

cases.n: Trinidad and Tobago — Sabga task force on children's homes, kept secret for 25 years
cases.victims_note: 30 to 40 children abused by one employee at St Dominic's Children's Home
cases.who: Children's homes incl. St Dominic's Children's Home and St Jude's School for Girls
cases.cover: Abuser at St Dominic's was asked to resign and allegedly helped into hospital work; report never published by government
cases.d: A task force appointed by the Cabinet in 1997 and chaired by Robert Sabga visited nine children's homes. It found that a male employee at St Dominic's Children's Home had repeatedly sexually abused some 30 to 40 children and, when discovered, was asked to resign and allegedly helped to find work at a hospital; it also recorded beatings at St Jude's School for Girls. The report was never published; the Trinidad Express published its findings in May 2022.
cases.cite: Report of the Cabinet-appointed Task Force on children's homes (Robert Sabga, chair), 1997, as published by the Trinidad Express, May 2022
